diagnostic_evidence.quote: On the other hand, for $n_0=0.25$, the policy related to $\J^2$ performs poorly since the mean TTP has more than halved if compared to the other treatment approaches.
We insist on the fact that in the rows marked as `Hyperbolic' we used $\tau_{TTP'}^\theta$.
the continuity of the mapping $\tau\mapsto s^\theta(\tau) + r^\theta(\tau)$ for every $\theta$ implies that $\tau_{\mathrm{TTP}}^\theta \leq \tau_{\mathrm{TTP'}}^\theta $.

issues.failure_explanation: The sentence claims the policy computed with the hyperbolic cost outperforms MTD and AT on average (mean TTP over the ensemble). The paper's own Table Sum_Hyp shows that for n_0=0.25 this policy's mean TTP is 102 days, less than half of MTD (210 days) and of 'On-Off' AT (213 days), and the results section itself concedes it performs poorly there; the claimed superiority holds only for n_0=0.5 and n_0=0.75. Moreover, the hyperbolic rows are scored with tau_TTP' (last time below the threshold), which by Remark rmk:TTPvsTTP' is always >= the first-crossing tau_TTP used for the benchmark rows, so even the favorable cases rest on a strictly more lenient metric. As written, the blanket sentence is false and materially misleading.

failure_location.quote: on average it outperforms MTD and AT in terms of `time to progression' (see \cref{table:MTD_AT1,table:Sum_Hyp})

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the sentence: state that the mean-TTP improvement holds for n_0 in {0.5, 0.75}, report the n_0=0.25 deterioration already documented in the body, and note that the hyperbolic rows are evaluated with tau_TTP'.
issues.overall_effect: The introduction's summary of the numerical study overstates what the experiments establish: the advertised average superiority of the ensemble-optimal (hyperbolic) policy is unsupported for n_0=0.25 and is partly an artifact of the weaker TTP' metric. The tables and formal results themselves stand.
issues.title: Intro overclaims average TTP superiority of the hyperbolic-cost policy
issues.why_classification: The results section already contains the contradicting numbers and the metric disclosure; the repair is a local qualification of one summary sentence with no change to any method, table, or formal result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and we can deduce that the set $\Delta_1$ is invariant.

issues.failure_explanation: On Delta_1 = {s=0} the reduced dynamics is dr/dtau = r_R_hat(1-r)r - d_T_hat r = r(r_R_hat - d_T_hat - r_R_hat r), which is nonnegative exactly for 0 <= r <= (r_R_hat - d_T_hat)/r_R_hat (when d_T_hat < r_R_hat), not up to r_R_hat/(r_R_hat + d_T_hat) as stated. The two thresholds coincide only when d_T_hat = 0. Counterexample: r_R_hat = d_T_hat = 1 and r = 0.4 < 1/2 gives dr/dtau = 0.4(0.6) - 0.4 = -0.16 < 0, contradicting the claimed nonnegativity on [0, r_R_hat/(r_R_hat+d_T_hat)]; if d_T_hat > r_R_hat the derivative is negative on the whole interval (0,1]. The displayed case split in the proof is therefore false as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the threshold to (r_R_hat - d_T_hat)/r_R_hat (with the appropriate sign statement when d_T_hat >= r_R_hat), or prove the invariance of Delta_1 directly from the endpoint signs dr/dtau|_{r=0}=0 and dr/dtau|_{r=1}=-d_T_hat <= 0.
issues.overall_effect: The intermediate sign analysis from which the invariance of Delta_1 is deduced is incorrect, so that deduction rests on a false premise as written. The conclusion of Lemma lem:domain_invariance remains true (dr/dtau = 0 at r=0 and dr/dtau = -d_T_hat <= 0 at r=1 already keep [0,1] invariant), hence the truncation argument, Lemma lem:extension, and the gradient formulas that rely on the lemma are not actually lost.
issues.title: False sign threshold in the proof of simplex invariance on Delta_1
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-line computational correction inside the proof; the lemma's statement and every result depending on it survive unchanged, so it is a short local fix with no mathematical loss.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we discretized the interval $[0.5,1]$ where $\hat r_R$ varies into $25$ equi\-spaced nodes with distance $0.02$. Hence, we set $U(0.5,1)\approx \frac{1}{25}\sum_{j=1}^{25} \delta_{\hat r_R^j}$, with $\hat r_R^j\in \{0.5, 0.52,\ldots,1\}$.

we divided the interval $[0.002,1]$ into $49$ nodes with a constant step equal to $0.002$. Then, we considered $U(0.002,0.1)\approx \frac{1}{49}\sum_{k=1}^{49} \delta_{\hat f_0^k}$, with $\hat f_0^k\in \{0.002, 0.004,\ldots,0.1\}$.
which has a support consisting of $N=1225$ points.

issues.failure_explanation: The grids as listed contain 26 values of r_R_hat (0.5, 0.52, ..., 1 with step 0.02) and 50 values of f_0_hat (0.002, ..., 0.1 with step 0.002), so the set in eq:Theta_N_simul has 26*50 = 1300 points; but eq:mu_N_simul assigns weights 1/25 and 1/49 and the text asserts a support of N = 1225 = 25*49 points, which corresponds to grids ending at 0.98 and 0.098, not at 1 and 0.1. Node counts, step sizes, endpoints, and weights are mutually inconsistent (the f_0_hat interval is also printed as [0.002,1] instead of [0.002,0.1]), so the discrete measure actually used in the experiments is not coherently specified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reconcile the counts with the grids (either use 26 and 50 nodes with weights 1/26 and 1/50 and N=1300, or drop the last nodes and keep 25, 49 and N=1225) and correct the [0.002,1] endpoint to [0.002,0.1].
issues.overall_effect: The exact ensemble underlying every numerical result (Tables MTD_AT1, Sum_Hyp, Off-On and all figures) is ambiguous as written, so the experiments are not exactly reproducible from the text; any consistent reading, however, yields an almost identical uniform ensemble.
issues.title: Discrete ensemble measure inconsistently specified (node counts vs grids vs N=1225)
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local editorial fix to the discretization paragraph; no proof, method, or qualitative conclusion changes under either consistent reading, so every substantive claim survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: At $\tau =0$, set {$u=0$} and keep it constant while $s^\theta(\tau) + r^\theta(\tau)<  1.2\, n_0$ (vacation period).
The TTP of `On-Off'~AT and `Off-On'~AT is $424$ days and $459$ days, respectively
We remark that in the experiments involving MTD and `On-Off' AT we observed $\tau_{\mathrm{TTP}}^\theta = \tau_{\mathrm{TTP'}}^\theta $ for every $\theta\in \Theta_N$
We insist on the fact that in the rows marked as `Hyperbolic' we used $\tau_{TTP'}^\theta$.

issues.failure_explanation: By construction, 'Off-On' AT keeps u=0 until the tumor reaches 1.2 n_0 (Step 1). In the simulated regime (u=0, d_T_hat=0), dn/dtau = (1-n)(s + r_R_hat r) >= r_R_hat (1-n) n > 0 for 0<n<1, so every trajectory strictly increases toward the carrying capacity and crosses the progression threshold 1.2 n_0 during the first vacation phase, for the simulated parameters within days-to-weeks (e.g., growing from 0.5 to 0.6). Hence the first-crossing time tau_TTP of eq:def_TTP is small for every theta and cannot equal the reported values (min 107-400 days, mean 217-589 days, and the 459 days quoted in fig:Off-On). Those numbers must be tau_TTP' (the last time below threshold, eq:def_TTP'), which the paper itself notes differs from tau_TTP whenever the tumor shrinks back below the threshold; yet, unlike the explicit disclosure for the hyperbolic rows of Table Sum_Hyp, no disclosure is made here, and the paper states tau_TTP = tau_TTP' only for MTD and 'On-Off' AT. As captioned, 'TTP' contradicts the paper's own definition.

failure_location.quote: Comparison in terms of Time-to-Progression (TTP) between `On-Off'~AT and `Off-On'~AT.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Disclose explicitly, as the paper already does for the hyperbolic rows of Table Sum_Hyp, that the 'Off-On' AT rows of Table Off-On and the value in fig:Off-On report tau_TTP'; with that statement the numbers and the TTP'-based comparison stand.
issues.overall_effect: The headline evaluation of the paper's proposed therapy (Table Off-On, fig:Off-On, and the downstream claim of 'improvement in almost every performance indicator') is computed with the strictly weaker TTP' metric while being labelled TTP; under the primary definition eq:def_TTP, 'Off-On' AT registers progression at the first treatment onset by design, so the comparison as stated is not supported by the reported values.
issues.title: 'Off-On' AT results are labelled TTP but must be TTP'
issues.why_classification: The least adequate repair is the same one-sentence metric disclosure the paper itself uses elsewhere; no recomputation or new argument is required and the comparative claims survive as statements about TTP'.
